specAcceptance.reason: This ticket defines schemas and deterministic fixtures; the empty-list UI and application state are implemented by later S06 work, not by the shared contract package.
nextAction ordering is a packages/domain pure function and is outside this schema-only ticket.
Approval invalidation after confirmation revocation is a domain state transition not implemented by this ticket.
Inbox read and resolution behavior requires application persistence and derived state, neither of which is part of this ticket.
Tenant-scoped API visibility and 404 behavior require authenticated runtime access; this ticket adds no API or storage.
Job activity creation and redaction require worker and activity behavior; this ticket only validates their data shapes.
Deadline inbox inclusion depends on persisted deadline state and derived inbox behavior, which are outside this ticket.
Archive write refusal is a domain state transition; no mutation path is implemented by the shared contract package.

V6-03 A01–A03 are covered at the shared schema and deterministic parsing layer. They do not exercise a persisted application command, repeated action against stale/failed application state, or persisted refresh/retry behavior because this ticket creates no such runtime path; the receipt states this scope explicitly.

Decision ACTIVITY-METADATA-BY-ACTION (user-selected): freeze a conservative per-action matrix in ACTIVITY_METADATA_KEYS_BY_ACTION. Keys are limited to non-negative version/count integers, constrained stage/provider/model identifiers, and registered ErrorCode values; job.succeeded and job.adopted require both provider and model identifiers for S06-A06. privacy.export and privacy.delete require empty metadata. Free-text reasons/messages, payloads, secrets, payment amounts, contact details, consent scope, and manifests are excluded. The contract README records the rule and the source matrix is packages/contracts/src/records.ts.

Preservation check: all 407 baseline untracked paths match; the check does not cover pre-existing tracked dirty changes. No commit, deployment, network call, model call, or real customer data operation was performed.
